legend: Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation in gamma heavy chain disease (<<30308>>): the serum protein electrophoresis lane (ELP) shows a distinct broad band (arrowhead), consistent with an M component. There is a corresponding band in the gamma lane (G), indicating that the M component is composed of gamma heavy chain; however, no corresponding bands are seen in either the kappa (K) or lambda (L) light chain lanes, which show only faint polyclonal patterns. (Other lane labels: A, alpha; M, mu.) FNA of a parotid mass (Giemsa) (<<30317>>) demonstrates a heterogeneous population of numerous small lymphocytes with round to slightly irregular nuclei, clumped chromatin, and moderate eccentric basophilic cytoplasm, indicative of plasmacytic differentiation. Also present are occasional epithelioid histiocytes with oval nuclei and abundant cytoplasm, seen on the right side of the image. Concurrent flow cytometry (<<30319>>) demonstrated a population of CD19+, CD20+ B cells (blue, bottom) that were negative for both kappa and lambda immunoglobulin light chains (blue, top).

Histological examination of this axillary lymph node biopsy in a 64-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus demonstrates architectural effacement with marked paracortical expansion associated with hypervascularity. The paracortical expansion consists of a monomorphic infiltrate of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with round nuclei, clumped chromatin, and moderate pink cytoplasm, including some cells with eccentric nuclei and paranuclear hof, overall consistent with plasmacytic differentiation (H&E) (<<30399>>). A stain for CD19 highlights residual follicles (left) and the paracortical lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate (right) (<<30400>>), which also stained positively for CD138 and IgG, and negatively for kappa and lambda light chains (not shown). The paracortical lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate shows a low Ki-67 proliferation index, of 5–10% (<<30402>>). Subsequent ipsilateral axillary lymph node biopsy performed three months later demonstrates complete architectural effacement consisting of lymphoid cells and a more prominent histiocytic proliferation forming small coalescent clusters; on high-power examination, there is an infiltrate of lymphoid cells with prominent plasmacytic features, including eccentric nuclei, clumped chromatin, and moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm, consistent with persistent disease (<<30404>>). The lymphoplasmacytic cells are positive for IRF4 (MUM1) (<<30405>>). Mitotic activity is more apparent than in the earlier biopsy (H&E), with a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 60% (<<30406>>). The lymphoplasmacytic cells are diffusely but weakly positive for IgG heavy chain by immunohistochemistry (<<30408>>), but they were negative for both kappa and lambda light chains (not shown).

Bone marrow evaluation of a 46-year-old man with a history of rheumatoid arthritis shows loose lymphoid aggregates consisting of small lymphocytes, plasmacytoid lymphocytes, and plasma cells (<<30412>>, <<30413>>). The lymphoplasmacytic cells are positive for CD138 (<<30414>>) and IgG heavy chain by immunohistochemistry (<<30415>>). In situ hybridization for kappa (<<30417>>) and lambda light chains highlights fewer plasma cells, in a different distribution from that of the IgG-expressing plasma cells (<<30418>>).

diagnosis: Gamma heavy chain disease involving an axillary lymph node
legend: Histological examination of this axillary lymph node biopsy (H&E) in a 64-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus demonstrates architectural effacement with marked paracortical expansion associated with hypervascularity. The cortex contains vague small follicles with clusters of epithelioid histiocytes outside of follicles adjacent to mantle zones. The paracortical expansion consists of a monomorphous infiltrate of small to medium-sized lymphoid cells with round nuclei, clumped chromatin, and moderate pink cytoplasm, including some cells with eccentric nuclei and paranuclear hofs, overall consistent with plasmacytic differentiation. Immunohistochemical analysis (not shown) demonstrated the paracortical lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate to coexpress CD19 and CD138 with diffuse staining for IgG, but negative for kappa or lambda light chains, consistent with gamma heavy chain disease.
